radiology_report:
Amsterdam UMC (location VUmc)
Radiology Dept
Date: 15 Dec 2024
Exam: mpMRI prostate

Clinical indication: Rising PSA (5.3 ng/mL), prior biopsy Gleason 3+4. Evaluate for focal lesion.

FINDINGS:
Prostate volume measures 48.0 mL. T2-weighted imaging demonstrates a focal area of low signal intensity in the peripheral zone, right posterior base, measuring approximately 12 mm in maximal dimension. This lesion demonstrates restricted diffusion on DWI (b=1400) and early enhancement on DCE sequences, consistent with a PI-RADS 4 lesion. No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion is identified. Lymph nodes are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 4 lesion, right posterior peripheral zone, ~12 mm.
PSA density: 0.11 ng/mL/mL.
Clinical T stage: cT2a.
csPCa predicted probability 0.40281674.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. van den Berg (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient presented with elevated PSA of 4.1 ng/mL. Digital rectal examination was unremarkable. Multiparametric MRI was arranged and biopsy was performed. Histology confirmed Gleason 3+4, ISUP GG2. Discussed options of active surveillance versus definitive treatment. Patient expressed preference for surveillance but requested regular follow-up. Referred to urology for shared decision-making.

pathology_report:
Biopsy performed 10 Sep 2023:
Histological examination of the prostate cores reveals adenocarcinoma, Gleason score 3+4, corresponding to ISUP grade group 2. The malignant glands exhibit an acinar growth pattern, partly fusing. No cribriform or intraductal patterns are identified. Perineural invasion is absent.

Biopsy performed 06 Dec 2024:
